scouting_text:
Sebastian Aho is off to a heater for Carolina — 4 goals and 4 assists in 5 games, 8 points, and he's doing it in just over 19 and a half minutes a night. The goals-per-60 number jumps off the page at 2.457, which is elite finishing volume for a center. He's also been a fixture on the power play, with 3 of his 4 goals and 4 of his 8 points coming with the man advantage. That's a guy who's clearly the triggerman on the top unit.

The even-strength profile is a little more muted. His RAPM sits at 0.07, basically league average, and the on-ice expected goals are a wash — 1.36 xGF per 60 against 1.41 xGA per 60. So the defensive side of his game has been leaky early, and he's not tilting the ice at fives the way you'd expect from a true No. 1 center. The 5 giveaways against zero takeaways backs that up; he's creating on offense but coughing up the biscuit.

Where he fits: Aho is Carolina's top-line pivot, the guy the whole forward group runs through. The counting stats say he's a finisher and a power-play weapon right now. The underlying numbers say there's room for the two-way game to catch up. If the even-strength play tightens and those giveaways come down, he's a legit top-tier center. For now, he's producing points in bunches and driving the PP — and that's a beauty of a start.
